- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly to reflect bearish sentiment’s diminishing impact.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5–10% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a mild downward bias (e.g., -1 to -3% of recent average).
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply a slight upward bias to compensate for lag.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher weight to recent sentiment if >0.3.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope to prevent overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive -1.00), model underreacts; add 2–5% upward adjustment to prevent premature bottoming.
